summary: A set of short named commands such as make dev, make test and make setup that wrap the longer project commands.
purpose: Gives developers one simple command for each common task, including first-time setup and resetting data.
why: Saves developers from remembering long Docker and pnpm commands.
how: Running make with a name runs the commands listed under it in order. The help command lists every command that has a description.
inputs: The command name typed by the developer, plus the environment file and Docker files.
outputs: Starts containers, installs packages, runs database steps and tests, and prints messages in the terminal.
risks: docker-clean removes all container data volumes. db-reset wipes the database and is marked destructive. Setup waits a fixed 5 seconds instead of checking that the database is ready.
debug: If setup fails, run the individual step that failed. If services are not running, use docker-logs. Confirm Docker is running.
